pr_comments:
> Most of the changes seem logical. I've runtime tested this without your dynpath hacks (I mean those comments I mention "please drop") and it seems to work just fine. Any reason you decided to added that?

Have you tried playing a stack from the home screen??
Here it works fine from the Movie menu without the DynPath hacks, but not from the home screen (in progress/recent etc..) as they pass a VideoDB url in Path.
Guys, please let me have a look at this issue. Not sure, but I think there could be a simpler fix possible. The changes made here seem a bit "invasive" so I'm hesitant to put this into v21.

@ksooo we've branched already, any PR targetting master is now effectively for v22 (anything for omega has to be backported). I agree this is too invasive for v21 although the changes from a logical POV are correct and perfectly fine for v22 at this point.

Probably we want a simple/localized fix for v21 even if it is some "hack", as long as properly fixed in master.

issue_context.title: File stacks only play first part of stack from home screen in v21
issue_context.body:
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
Here is a clear and concise description of what the problem is:

File stacks only play first part of stack from home screen.

## Expected Behavior
Here is a clear and concise description of what was expected to happen:

The entire stack should play.

## Actual Behavior

Only the first part plays.

## Possible Fix

PR #24813 

### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

Create a file stack (in this case 4 parts about 30m each)
Play from the home screen

![image](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/99039295/a540c350-968f-4027-8ec6-3b96f6cdce67)

(The info at the bottom is correct but the progress bar reflects only the first item).

On the play progress bar you can see it's only the first part.

![image](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/99039295/8429dbf6-2f68-4587-bc88-4bbcc74dd0aa)

In v20 (and with proposed fix) the whole stack is properly played.

![image](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/assets/99039295/baa21fb7-bd25-4b4d-a69d-5b8c6f1366d2)

### Debuglog

https://paste.kodi.tv/xocifelemo.kodi

### Screenshots 

As above.

review_comments: Just saying that all (?) `CFileItem::Is`methods working on `m_strPath`. With this change this method now is the exception. Not saying this is wrong, but looks like a big inconsistency. Maybe we should at least add a comment explaining why this method is different from the others.

I think in the end, if we think hard enough about obscure use-cases the others may be in fact wrong. It's not by chance that all these misbehaviours happen we we start moving constant paths to playlists (e.g. strm files) or paths are served from plugins which need resolution.
I mean it may cause regressions but from a logical POV IsStack applied to a CFileItem should look always first to the dynpath (may have been resolved) and only after that to the path (signature of the item). If that is not the intended behaviour the client code should invoke `URIUtils::IsStack` directly with the path it wishes to check.
I think the comment may not be necessary here

> if we think hard enough about obscure use-cases the others may be in fact wrong.

I tend to agree.
